summary: Duplicate Alert Suppression Window: POST /api/alerts returns the existing active alert (200 + X-Duplicate-Suppressed: true) instead of creating a new row when an active alert with the same Title (case-insensitive) and Severity was created within a configurable window (default 15 min).

acceptance_criteria.text: POST /api/alerts, when an active alert with the same Title (case-insensitive) and same Severity was created within the suppression window, does not insert a new row.
On suppression the response is 200 OK with the existing alert as the body and response header 'X-Duplicate-Suppressed: true'.
When no matching alert is within the window, POST /api/alerts still creates the alert and returns 201 Created (no X-Duplicate-Suppressed header).
The suppression window in minutes is read from configuration in appsettings.json (not hardcoded); default value in appsettings.json is 15.
An alert with the same Title but a different Severity is not suppressed (new alert created, 201).
A prior matching alert that is inactive (IsActive = false) does not suppress; a new alert is created (201).
A matching active alert created before the window start (older than the configured minutes) does not suppress; a new alert is created (201).

scope_anchors: IAlertRepository + AlertRepository (new duplicate lookup: Title ci + Severity + IsActive + CreatedDate >= now - window)
Program.cs options binding + appsettings.json new section
constraints: Scope exceeds the 5-source-file cap deliberately: the story crosses Controller, Service, Repository interface/impl, options and configuration.
Keep layering Controller -> IAlertService -> IAlertRepository -> AlertDbContext; controller stays HTTP-only (maps result to 200/201 and sets header); entities never leave the service layer.
Window comes from IOptions-bound configuration (e.g. 'AlertSuppression:DuplicateWindowMinutes'); no hardcoded 15 in code; validate at startup (non-negative; 0 disables suppression).
Use TimeProvider (already injected) for 'now'; CreatedDate is UTC.

Duplicate lookup must be a parameterized EF query (no raw SQL); compare Title case-insensitively consistent with existing repository search (ToLower); Title is trimmed in ToEntity so compare against the trimmed request title.
No schema change or migration expected; index review only if standards require (existing IsActive index).
Suppression must not alter validation: invalid requests still return 400 before the lookup.
Changing IAlertService.CreateAsync return type requires updating existing tests and the controller test.
coverage_goals: Every acceptance criterion AC1-AC7 covered by at least one passing test; suppress/create branches in service and controller, and the repository lookup filters (title case, severity, active, window boundary), covered at behavior level.
missing_facts: Response body shape on suppression (assumed same AlertResponse of the existing alert; no Location header)
unresolved_questions: Window boundary: assumed an alert counts as 'within' when CreatedDate >= now - window (inclusive).
If several matches exist, assumed the most recent one is returned.
Window of 0 assumed to disable suppression; negative values rejected at startup.
Concurrent identical POSTs can still both insert (no unique constraint/lock); accepted as best-effort suppression unless a human requires stronger guarantees.
